data.narrative:
Tytan Technologies is a Series A-stage defense and security company founded by Balazs Nagy and Batuhan Yumurtaci that has raised €30M to date. The valuation analysis draws from a comparable universe of 10 companies: 2 public peers (DRSHF, IDEAFORGE.NS) and 8 private-stage firms including Stark Defence, Castelion, Singularity, NODA AI, and Anduril Industries.

Two valuation methods were applied. Stage-progression analysis uses the €30M total raised as a baseline and applies a 2.0x step-up multiplier typical for Series A advancement, yielding $60M. Peer-median analysis examines four same-sector, same-stage comparables with valuations ranging from $125M (NODA AI) to $4.0B (Stark Defence). The median of this peer set is $700M, reflecting substantial heterogeneity in the sample.

Triangulating these methods produces a valuation range of $51M (low) to $805M (high), with a median of $380M. The wide dispersion—spanning nearly two orders of magnitude—reflects the high variance in peer valuations within the Defense & Security frontier-tech category. The stage-progression method anchors the low end, while peer comparables drive higher estimates. Key uncertainties include which peer comparables are truly analogous to Tytan's specific technology and market positioning, and whether the company's capital efficiency and product maturity align with peers at the median or extremes of the range.
